name: eps Ind B

grid.orientation: north up, east left; same grid as the time-lapse frames
grid.data_layout: base64 Float32 little-endian, rows from the bottom (y = 0) up; NaN = no data

units: MJy/sr, zodiacal light and median background removed
how_to_read: Each detector array sees a different range of infrared wavelengths (D1 shortest, D6 longest). A real moving object shifts the same way in every detector; a defect appears in only one. Shifts smaller than about 2 arcseconds (a third of a pixel) are within our measurement precision. If another source is brighter than the object at some wavelengths, the measurement there follows that source: for WISE 0855, a hot background star dominates D1 to D4, so only D5 and D6 show the brown dwarf moving.
data_credit: NASA SPHEREx via NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA); target data from SIMBAD (CDS)
